successors.name: Sena dynasty
successors.text: the Pala remnant: Varendra and Radha, Gauda taken by Ballala Sena, the rest 'annexed sometime after 1165'

ledger.x: 750: the chiefs of Gauda elect Gopala.

c. 791: Dharmapala takes Kannauj and sets his brother on its throne. Dharmapala was 'invading the kingdom of Kannauj around 791', defeated Indrayudha and installed his brother Chakrayudha as a vassal (the Khalimpur plate, regnal year 32, records it without a CE date).
800: the campaign over; no page gives a later date and the Rashtrakutas did not stay.

c. 810: the king of Pragjyotisha submits to Devapala. 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala'; the Devapala page lists the invasion of Pragjyotisha, also undated. 810 is Devapala's accession on Majumdar's column (810-c. 850; Sircar 812, Ganguly 806), the bridge year of…

c. 860: the Odisha tint ends. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa'. 860 is Narayanapala's accession on Sircar's column (860-917; Majumdar 854, Chowdhury 866, Ganguly 873, which the ruler strip follows) and the year kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/15 uses. An earlier version stood at…

c. 860: the Pragjyotisha tint ends. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa'; 'Encouraged by the Pala decline, the King Harjara of Assam assumed imperial titles'. 860 as for Orissa and as kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/15, the mirror. An earlier version stood at 840.
947: east Bengal is out of Pala hands.
1056: the west of Cliopatria's Kamarupa shape falls to the Pala shape (north and east Bengal edge, Meghalaya and Goalpara side, 24,026 km2).

c. 1077: Ramapala builds a new capital at Ramavati. 'He ruled from a new capital at Ramavati, which remained the Pala capital until the dynasty's end'; the page gives no year, 1077 is the infobox start of his reign.

c. 1100: Ramapala takes western Kamarupa. 'He brought Kamarupa and Rarh under his control', undated. 1100 and the region are those of kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/26 (confidence 2 there, the end of Jaya Pala's reign); here a bridge inside Ramapala's reign, confidence…
1159: the Senas hold a part of Varendra.

wars.name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
wars.outcome: Dhruva beat Dharmapala in the Doab (home in 790); Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj around 791; Govinda III received Dharmapala's submission in 800; 'In 816, Nagabhata II invaded the Doab, and defeated king Chakrayudha'.

wars.name: Pratihara advance on Bihar
wars.outcome: Nagabhata II defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr and took the plain 'as far as Bihar from the Palas'; Bhoja later 'defeated the Pala emperor Narayanapala after Devapala's death'.

wars.name: Mahipala I's recovery of Bengal
wars.outcome: 'Mahipala I recovered northern and eastern Bengal within three years of ascending the throne in 978 CE.'

wars.name: Chola invasions of Bengal
wars.outcome: Rajendra Chola I 'frequently invaded Bengal from 1021 to 1023 CE to get Ganges water'; Mahipala I's rule was 'temporarily hampered'.

wars.name: Varendra rebellion
wars.outcome: Mahipala II was killed, Shurapala ruled two years, and Ramapala recovered Varendra from Bhima and Divya; none of the events is dated on the page.

wars.name: Sena conquest of Pala Bengal
wars.outcome: By 1159 the Senas held Vanga and a part of Varendra; Ballala Sena took Gaur; 'the Palas were ousted in totality' sometime after 1165.

wars.name: Pala-Gahadavala conflict over Munger
wars.outcome: 'Madanapala captured Munger from the Gahadavalas'; undated, so the span is his reign (Ganguly 1143-1161).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded on the pages opened; the Gangetic plain frontier with the Pratiharas and the Bengal frontier with the Kambojas, Chandras and Senas are approximate throughout.
